title: Healthy people, healthy climate? Understanding the connection of well-being (SDG 3) and climate action (SDG 13) through health psychology.
abstract: Growing recognition of the interdependence between human health, climate change and environmental sustainability has highlighted the importance of understanding how climate-friendly behaviours can simultaneously promote individual health, climate and environmental protection. Concepts such as One Health, Planetary Health and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) emphasize that human well-being depends on healthy ecosystems, a stable climate and supportive social systems. Yet achieving these goals remains challenging because many climate-friendly behaviours involve trade-offs between short-term individual benefits and long-term collective outcomes. This Special Issue addresses these challenges at the intersection of SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) and SDG 13 (Climate Action). The contributing papers span topics including mobility, nutrition, climate emotions, self-regulation, social norms and behaviour-change interventions. Collectively, the papers demonstrate that health and climate outcomes are deeply interconnected but that co-benefits are conditional on psychological mechanisms, social contexts and structural opportunities. Based on this evidence, we propose an integrative framework linking environmental conditions, psychological processes and behavioural responses, as well as health and climate outcomes for researchers, practitioners and policy-makers. To achieve SDG 3 and SDG 13 together, psychology must promote well-being not as an end point in itself but as a foundation and driver for responsible and sustainable behaviour, using evidence-based behaviour-change theories, techniques and interventions.
